newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares ease at close on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares ease at close on profit taking.

text.p: Singapore shares trimmed gains late on Friday as investors, heartened after several bullish sessions, took profit ahead of the weekend, dealers said. Demand for selected blue chip stocks perked up, but volume stayed firmly in the Malaysian over-the-counter stable.
"There was a wee bit of foreign buying in blue chips, which helped the index, but punters in second liners are still having a field day," a foreign securities firm dealer said.
The Straits Times Industrials Index drifted down 2.22 points to 2,252.46, and the UOB-OTC index fell 1.32 to 1,311.78. Volume was a brisk 453.7 million shares overall at the close.
Dealers said heavy trading in Malaysian Clob issues had sobered slightly compared with Thursday, when overall volume hit a three-year high of 746 million shares.
But more upside potential was projected for the short-term, aided by the bull run in Wall Street and presence of foreign funds in the recently re-rated Singapore bourse.
"There are not big sellers around. Foreigners are still net buyers," another dealer with a local firm said.
A broad range of blue chips were favoured with net gainers like SPH foreign, up Singapore $1.00 at S$30.10, and UOB foreign, up S$0.60 at S$17.30.
